articles.title: India's First World Happiness Summit Concludes in Bengaluru - Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: India's First World Happiness Summit Concludes in Bengaluru Shilpa Shetty, Arjun Kapoor, Dr. Kiran Bedi, Dr. Saamdu Chetri and Sonu Sharma join Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi to reframe happpiness around Pleasure, Peace and Purpose By : DC Correspondent Update: 2026-09-30 08:01 GMT India’s first World Happpiness Summit concluded today at New Horizon College of Engineering, Bengaluru, drawing a full-day audience into a conversation the country rarely pauses for: what does it truly take to be happy? Hosted by Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi, the Happpiness Ambassador, the summit brought together voices from entertainment, public life, entrepreneurship, spirituality, wellness and social leadership, and closed with a collective resolve to make Bengaluru the world’s happiest city. Positioned as India’s first World Happpiness Summit, the day-long gathering was built around the idea that lasting happiness rests on three pillars, Pleasure, Peace and Purpose, the three Ps that give the brand its distinctive spelling. In a city celebrated as India’s technology and innovation capital, the summit sought to add a new dimension to Bengaluru’s identity, one that places wellbeing and fulfilment alongside ambition and growth. The morning session opened with the lighting of the lamp and an invocation, followed by Dr. Kiran Bedi on the Fundamentals of Happiness and Arjun Kapoor on The Secret of Happiness. A panel on Success and Happiness brought together Govind Mahtani, Shareen, Nikhil Kamath and Hema Sardesai, while a second panel explored the Manifestation of Happiness through Attraction with Dr. Amiett Kumar, Tarun Mishra, Rohit Khandelwal and Bhupendra Singh. Dr. Saamdu Chetri, a pioneer of Bhutan’s Gross National Happiness philosophy, offered a global perspective on measuring wellbeing over wealth. The afternoon carried the momentum forward with Sonu Sharma on How to Be Happy Every Day and Aisshwarya DKS on The Science of Happiness. A panel on The Art of Being Happy featured Sruthi Hariharan, Preetika Rao, Archika Sudhanshu, Dr. Aadhyaa Kumar and Renuka Goswami. Bringing the marquee sessions to a close, Shilpa Shetty spoke on The 3 Keys to Eternal Happiness, weaving together the wellness and positivity that have long defined her public life. Through the day, the summit also presented the Champion Awards, honouring individuals and organisations that foster positive work environments and champion the wellbeing of their people, extending the happiness conversation from the personal to the workplace. Reflecting on the day, Happpy AiR – Atman in Ravi, the Happpiness Ambassador said, “Today, hundreds of people came together not to chase happiness, but to experience it, and that is the shift we set out to create. Happiness is not a reward we earn at the end of a long climb. It is a way of living, made of Pleasure, Peace and Purpose. If Bengaluru can lead the world in technology and enterprise, it can just as surely lead the world in happiness. This summit is not a conclusion, it is the beginning of a larger movement to make this a Happy World.” Speaking at the summit, Dr. Kiran Bedi said, “Before you desire something,...

articles.title: Neeru-Kynan secure India's first -ever Asian Games trap mixed team event gold
articles.content: AICHI-NAGOYA (Japan): The Indian shooting duo of Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai secured a gold medal in the mixed trap team shooting event at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Wednesday, also establishing a new Games record in the process. Neeru, who had earlier secured a historic women’s trap individual gold, along with Kynan, had a score of 34, going past the Asian Games record of 30 (set by Qatar earlier this year). The silver medal went to Qatar (32), and China (23) took home the bronze. This is India’s first-ever gold medal in Trap Mixed Team event. This is India’s ninth gold medal at the Asian Games and third this day. This is also India’s 56th Asian Games 2026 medal, having won nine golds, 21 silver medals and 26 bronze medals. This also marks the 15th medal by India’s shooting contingent, having won three golds, eight silvers and four bronze medals. 🎯 ONE RANGE. TWO STORIES. ONE GOLDEN FINISH. 🇮🇳🥇 Kynan Chenai and Neeru Dhanda have delivered another shooting gold for India at Aichi-Nagoya 2026. They were only 4th after qualification. But the medal round changed everything. For Kynan, this was a comeback. After missing… pic.twitter.com/Zz1Y9PN4Tq — Anil Bansal (@dilseanilbansal) September 30, 2026 Neeru produced a dominant performance to win the women’s individual trap gold medal on Tuesday. Neeru maintained her composure in rainy conditions to finish on top of the eight-shooter final with a score of 26, according to ESPN. China’s Sun Yunong and Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik finished with 21 points each, while Qatar’s Ray Bassil took fourth place with 16 points. More Read ‘Inaugurating the era of Super Intelligence’: Trump signs order officially replacing term AI with SI ‘Don’t mess with us’: Netanyahu warns enemies of pre-election attack threat Neeru’s historic gold medal win marked a landmark moment for Indian shooting as she became the country’s first woman to win an individual Asian Games gold in trap shooting. She also set an Asian record on her Games debut in qualification, missing just two shots out of 30 to finish with 28. Earlier on Tuesday, Neeru had also won silver alongside Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer in the women’s trap team event. India finished with 328 points, behind gold medallists China (346), while Kuwait took bronze with 325. Neeru was India’s top performer in the team event, scoring 118 out of 125. Coming to more gold medals today, in archery, the Indian women’s compound team comprising Jyothi Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep defeated China 238-234 to win the gold medal. Earlier, the trio had beaten South Korea 234-233 in the semifinal. Chikitha Taniparthi and Sahil Jadhav also advanced to the compound mixed team final after edging Thailand 156-155 in a thrilling semifinal. Chikitha and Sahil booked a spot in the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics with their title win. articles.title: How India's First CEC Conducted First Election & Registered 17.3 Cr Voters Without Tech
articles.content: Most Indians have probably never heard of Sukumar Sen. They should have. Sen was India’s first Chief Election Commissioner. Appointed in 1950, he was the man entrusted with one of the most extraordinary administrative exercises in modern history: creating India’s first electoral rolls and conducting its first general election. Think about the India he was working in. There was almost no technology. No computers. No Aadhaar. No mobile phones. No digital databases. India had just emerged from Partition. The population was around 36.5 crore and literacy was only 16.6 percent. Yet the Election Commission had identified and enrolled more than 17.3 crore voters for the first general election. People physically went out, village by village, locality by locality, often door to door, to find citizens and put their names on the electoral roll. And here is something remarkable. The central instinct was inclusion. Not deletion. Find the citizen. Register the citizen. Give the citizen a place in India’s new democracy. Even when social customs prevented many women from giving their own names, Sukumar Sen insisted that women should be registered in their own names rather than as somebody’s wife or somebody’s mother. The Election Commission records that large numbers of such entries had to be corrected. ￼ This was the spirit in which India built its democracy. Nehru, Ambedkar, Rajendra Prasad and the Constituent Assembly created the constitutional foundation for universal adult suffrage. Sukumar Sen and the Election Commission turned that promise into an electoral system that could actually work on the ground. And that achievement deserves perspective. The first Indian general election was the largest democratic exercise the world had seen, conducted through universal adult suffrage in a country that was poor, overwhelmingly rural and overwhelmingly illiterate. ￼ So the next time someone asks, “What did Nehru do for India?”, remember this. The founding generation did something extraordinary. They did not inherit a functioning democracy. They built one. They understood that democracy begins not with the politician. It begins with the voter. Dear Readers, As an independent media platform, we do not take advertisements from governments and corporate houses. articles.title: Hyderabad EON Space Labs gets patent for miniaturised space imaging system - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Hyderabad Eon Space Labs Gets Patent For Miniaturised Space Imaging System Hyderabad EON Space Labs gets patent for miniaturised space imaging system Hyderabad-based EON Space Labs has secured a patent for MIRA, a miniaturised space telescope-based imaging system. Weighing 502 grams, the system is designed to provide high-definition multispectral Earth observation imagery for commercial applications across agriculture, mining, marine and insurance. By Telangana Today Published Date - 29 September 2026, 03:26 PM Hyderabad: EON Space Labs, a Hyderabad-based deeptech company developing advanced electro-optical imaging systems, has been granted a patent for its miniaturised space telescope-based imaging system. MIRA is an advanced imaging system, integrated with TakeMe2Space’s MOI-1A satellite — India’s first orbital computing satellite slated for launch on board the SpaceX Transporter-18 rocket on October 1. MIRA marked its first orbital flight attempt earlier this year in January on board ISRO’s PSLV-C62 mission. While an upper-stage anomaly prevented payload deployment, the mission successfully validated MIRA’s mechanical integration, spaceflight packaging, and hardware readiness. Building on this, EON Space Labs is also accelerating its flight heritage roadmap with another upcoming orbital deployment aboard ISRO’s Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV). Codenamed MIRA, it is also certified space-grade as per NASA standards, delivering high-definition multispectral EO imagery in an ultra-compact form factor. Weighing a mere 502 grams, MIRA enables satellite operators to offer commercial EO services across agriculture, marine, mining, supply-chain management, and insurance.
